narrative.overview: Coaster Hub should feel like the map you are handed at the gate: clear, friendly, and easy to find your way around, with the rides as the point. Calm, flat pages divided by hairlines and pale tinted bands; one bright ride yellow saved for the thing you came to do. Components are allowed to play: rounded shapes and park-themed touches like the admission ticket, coaster icons and the count that ticks up.
keyCharacteristics: Light and dark are both first-class; every color is a token defined for both.
Flat surfaces, hairline borders and pale signal-blue tints carry the structure.
Ride yellow means "do something" and nothing else.
Numbers are bold, tabular and blue; their labels are tiny small caps.
Park-themed shapes (ticket, timeline track, skyline) over generic UI chrome.
Mobile first: the phone layout is the primary one, desktop second.

rules.name: The One Yellow Rule
rules.body: Ride yellow is the "do something" color. One yellow control per view where possible, never yellow text on paper, never yellow as decoration.

rules.name: The Tokens Only Rule
rules.body: Colors come from the :root custom properties, defined for both themes.

rules.name: The Grey Means Gone Rule
rules.body: A defunct coaster's name and numbers go muted grey, sitewide.

rules.name: The Small Caps Under Big Numbers Rule
rules.body: A figure is always big, bold and blue with a tiny uppercase label beneath it.

rules.name: The Flat By Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. Add a tint band before reaching for a shadow; add a hairline before reaching for a fill.

dos: Do use the :root tokens for every color and check both themes.
Do keep Ride Yellow for the one main action on a view.
Do give every figure a tiny uppercase label beneath it.
Do reach for a park-themed shape (ticket, track, skyline) when a component needs personality.
Do bump the ?v= on style.css, lists.css and app.js in every page when they change.
Do honor prefers-reduced-motion: the count tick and page slides skip it.
donts: Don't use gradients on text, glows, or glass as decoration.
Don't put a transparent button over the skyline; outline buttons get a Panel fill.
Don't use CSS shorthands (background, font) that reset longhands set elsewhere.
Don't add a heading-sized "eyebrow" label above a heading.
Don't invent numbers, testimonials or placeholder data on any page.
Don't nest anything that must escape it (menus, popovers) inside .hero; it is overflow:hidden.
